From 8b07e990fb254fcbaa919616ac77f981cb48c73d Mon Sep 17 00:00:00 2001
From: Iwona Winiarska <iwona.winiarska@intel.com>
Date: Wed, 4 Aug 2021 01:48:19 +0200
Subject: [PATCH] soc: aspeed: p2a-ctrl: Fix boundary check for mmap

The check mixes pages (vm_pgoff) with bytes (vm_start, vm_end) on one
side of the comparison, and uses resource address (rather than just the
resource size) on the other side of the comparison.
This can allow malicious userspace to easily bypass the boundary check and
map pages that are located outside memory-region reserved by the driver.

Fixes: 01c60dcea9f7 ("drivers/misc: Add Aspeed P2A control driver")
Cc: stable@vger.kernel.org
Signed-off-by: Iwona Winiarska <iwona.winiarska@intel.com>
Reviewed-by: Andrew Jeffery <andrew@aj.id.au>
Tested-by: Andrew Jeffery <andrew@aj.id.au>
Reviewed-by: Joel Stanley <joel@aj.id.au>
Signed-off-by: Joel Stanley <joel@jms.id.au>

diff --git a/drivers/soc/aspeed/aspeed-p2a-ctrl.c b/drivers/soc/aspeed/aspeed-p2a-ctrl.c
index b60fbeaffcbd..20b5fb2a207c 100644
--- a/drivers/soc/aspeed/aspeed-p2a-ctrl.c
+++ b/drivers/soc/aspeed/aspeed-p2a-ctrl.c
@@ -110,7 +110,7 @@ static int aspeed_p2a_mmap(struct file *file, struct vm_area_struct *vma)
 	vsize = vma->vm_end - vma->vm_start;
 	prot = vma->vm_page_prot;
 
-	if (vma->vm_pgoff + vsize > ctrl->mem_base + ctrl->mem_size)
+	if (vma->vm_pgoff + vma_pages(vma) > ctrl->mem_size >> PAGE_SHIFT)
 		return -EINVAL;
 
 	/* ast2400/2500 AHB accesses are not cache coherent */
-- 
2.25.1

### Modifications in Each File

**File: `drivers/soc/aspeed/aspeed-p2a-ctrl.c`**
- The boundary check in the `aspeed_p2a_mmap` function was modified. 
- The original condition checked if the sum of `vma->vm_pgoff` and `vsize` (which is in bytes) exceeded the sum of `ctrl->mem_base` and `ctrl->mem_size` (which is a resource address).
- The modified condition now checks if the sum of `vma->vm_pgoff` and the number of pages in the virtual memory area (`vma_pages(vma)`) exceeds half of `ctrl->mem_size` shifted right by `PAGE_SHIFT` (which converts the size to pages).

### Relationships
- The modification addresses a security vulnerability where the original boundary check could allow userspace to map memory pages outside the reserved memory region. 
- By correcting the comparison to ensure both sides are in terms of pages, the patch enhances the integrity of memory mapping operations in the Aspeed P2A control driver, thereby preventing potential exploitation by malicious users.

Here is the commit message:
soc: aspeed: p2a-ctrl: Fix boundary check for mmap

The check mixes pages (vm_pgoff) with bytes (vm_start, vm_end) on one
side of the comparison, and uses resource address (rather than just the
resource size) on the other side of the comparison.
This can allow malicious userspace to easily bypass the boundary check and
map pages that are located outside memory-region reserved by the driver.

Fixes: 01c60dcea9f7 ("drivers/misc: Add Aspeed P2A control driver")
Cc: stable@vger.kernel.org
Signed-off-by: Iwona Winiarska <iwona.winiarska@intel.com>
Reviewed-by: Andrew Jeffery <andrew@aj.id.au>
Tested-by: Andrew Jeffery <andrew@aj.id.au>
Reviewed-by: Joel Stanley <joel@aj.id.au>
Signed-off-by: Joel Stanley <joel@jms.id.au>

Here is the root cause:
The bug was caused by a mix-up between page offsets (vm_pgoff) and byte sizes (vm_start, vm_end) in the boundary check, along with using a resource address instead of just the resource size. This allowed userspace to bypass the boundary check and potentially map memory pages outside the reserved region, leading to security vulnerabilities.

Here is the patch:
 
 static int aspeed_p2a_mmap(struct file *file, struct vm_area_struct *vma)
 {
 	unsigned long vsize;
 	pgprot_t prot;
 	struct aspeed_p2a_user *priv = file->private_data;
 	struct aspeed_p2a_ctrl *ctrl = priv->parent;
 
 	if (ctrl->mem_base == 0 && ctrl->mem_size == 0)
 		return -EINVAL;
 
 	vsize = vma->vm_end - vma->vm_start;
 	prot = vma->vm_page_prot;
 
-	if (vma->vm_pgoff + vsize > ctrl->mem_base + ctrl->mem_size)
+	if (vma->vm_pgoff + vma_pages(vma) > ctrl->mem_size >> PAGE_SHIFT)
 		return -EINVAL;
 
 	/* ast2400/2500 AHB accesses are not cache coherent */
 	prot = pgprot_noncached(prot);
 
 	if (remap_pfn_range(vma, vma->vm_start,
 		(ctrl->mem_base >> PAGE_SHIFT) + vma->vm_pgoff,
 		vsize, prot))
 		return -EAGAIN;
 
 	return 0;
 }

```c

```
Reason:
This statement incorrectly mixes page offsets (`vm_pgoff`) with byte sizes (`vm_start`, `vm_end`) and uses the resource address (`ctrl->mem_base`) instead of just the resource size (`ctrl->mem_size`). This allows userspace to bypass the boundary check and map memory pages outside the reserved region.

The code statements that fix the bug are:
```c
if (vma->vm_pgoff + vma_pages(vma) > ctrl->mem_size >> PAGE_SHIFT)
```
Reason:
This statement correctly uses the number of pages (`vma_pages(vma)`) instead of the byte size (`vsize`) and compares it against the resource size in pages (`ctrl->mem_size >> PAGE_SHIFT`). This ensures that the boundary check accurately reflects the reserved memory region, preventing userspace from mapping unauthorized memory pages.
